title: SAML session lifecycle: JIT account mapping, MFA expectation headers, and logout propagation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement final session lifecycle semantics for SAML SSO at Redwood Inference. Scope covers JIT provisioning behavior and attribute-to-role mapping for RBAC v2, how SAML-authenticated sessions surface MFA expectations to downstream services, logout semantics for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, re-auth and step-up rules, and the audit events that must be emitted for compliance. Deliverables: policy document, authn-context mapping table, server-side enforcement changes, updated audit schema, tests against our SAML test IdP, and admin console controls to terminate sessions and revoke JIT-provisioned accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc specifying TTLs, idle/absolute session timeouts, and re-auth triggers is reviewed and signed off by Security and Product
JIT provisioning mapping supports RBAC v2 role assignment via SAML attributes and safe fallback to 'pending' role for manual approval
MFA expectation from IdP (AuthnContext or custom attribute) is surfaced via a stable header/claim to internal services and enforced for step-up endpoints
SP-initiated logout and IdP-initiated logout both revoke session server-side and emit audit events with user, session_id, trigger (SP/IdP), and relay_state
Admin Console can list active SAML sessions, filter by user/org, and force logout with immediate audit log entry
End-to-end integration tests validating session revocation, JIT account flags, and audit lines pass in CI against the SAML test IdP
implementation_notes: Extend session store schema to include: session_origin (saml-sp, saml-idp, password), saml_attributes_snapshot, authn_context_identifier, mfa_required_flag, jti token for revocation propagation
On JIT provisioning, run attribute->role rules from RBAC v2 engine; if mapping incomplete, create account with 'provision_pending' tag and emit 'saml.jit.created.pending' audit event
Define a single internal claim/header 'X-RW-MFA-EXPECT' with values 'none', 'mfa', 'webauthn' derived from AuthnContextClassRef or SAML attribute 'mfaLevel'

Logout handling: SP-initiated LogoutRequest must find session by NameID or session_id, mark session revoked, send 200 to SP, and write 'saml.logout.sp' audit event. IdP-initiated Logout must accept LogoutRequest at /saml/idp/logout and revoke any matching sessions and emit 'saml.logout.idp'

Re-auth policy: sensitive endpoints (billing/export, admin console user management, RBAC role edit) should require session.authn_context >= 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:TimeSyncToken' or force step-up flow; implement middleware that inspects authn_context_identifier
Audit schema additions: event_type, actor_id, subject_id, session_id, session_origin, saml_relay_state, authn_context_identifier, attribute_diff (stringified), ip, user_agent, timestamp

Admin UI: add 'Terminate SAML Session' action which calls /admin/sessions/revoke with session_id and reason; ensure it invalidates server cache and propagates to any regional runtimes via existing revocation pubsub

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect role mapping on JIT can over-grant permissions. Mitigation: default to provision_pending, require manual approval for high-privilege roles and add automated alerting for mappings that target admin-level roles.

Risk: Logout storms when IdP triggers mass logout. Mitigation: rate-limit logout processing per org and use async revocation with best-effort immediate cache invalidation plus eventual consistency guarantees. Emit aggregate audit summaries rather than per-session for large bulk revocations.

Risk: MFA expectation mismatch between IdP and Redwood services. Mitigation: document supported AuthnContext URIs and provide a compatibility mapping table; expose a diagnostic header with raw authn_context for debugging.
Risk: Audit log volume growth. Mitigation: add retention and tiering policy and allow org-level opt-in for high-fidelity logs; default to standard retention for most events
